title: Filter Orders by Date
description:
Write a query to return all orders placed **on or after September 1, 2026**. Return `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, and `status`.

**Table: orders**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| order_date | DATE |
| status | VARCHAR |

In production you would typically replace the literal date with `CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 101, '2026-09-01', 'shipped'), (2, 102, '2026-09-10', 'delivered'), (3, 103, '2026-08-15', 'delivered'), (4, 104, '2026-09-20', 'processing'), (5, 105, '2026-07-30', 'delivered'), (6, 106, '2026-09-22', 'shipped'), (7, 107, '2026-08-01', 'delivered');
solution_sql: SELECT id, customer_id, order_date, status FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-09-01'

test_cases.description: Returns 4 orders placed on or after 2026-09-01

hints: Compare a DATE column to a date literal string like `'2026-09-01'` using `>=`, `>`, `<`, or `<=`.
Use `CURRENT_DATE` (or `NOW()`) in real applications instead of a hard-coded date to stay relative to today.
explanation: `WHERE order_date >= '2026-09-01'` filters rows to only those on or after the given date. DATE comparisons work just like numeric comparisons in SQL.
